items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I met the drummer whose name was Ed Shaughnessy and we went to the Florida Club to have a drink with he and Roy.

ctx.x: The new musicians that I did not know but had the opportunity to meet were Ernie Royal, a trumpetist, Alvin McCain, a tenor man, Butch Ballard a drummer that Duke had engaged to play the serious drum parts while Sonny featured on certain numbers that called for his showmanship. I didn't know Wendell Marshall, the bass player, but Lily and I went to four concerts and eventually we became acquainted with all the musicians I had not known before and that was the first time that I had heard Duke and his men so many…

Not long after Duke left Rome, Roy Eldridge came for one concert with Benny Goodman. It was a small combo which I did not hear, but I met the drummer whose name was Ed Shaughnessy and we went to the Florida Club to have a drink with he and Roy. They told me that "Toots" Thielemans, the guitar and harmonica player from Belgium was with the group. I knew of "Toots" but had not met him. It was a nice feeling to meet my ole colleague Roy in Rome where we had no idea we would meet when we played together in Teddy…

Most of the refugees were coming from behind the Iron curtain and were artists. One of them whose name I don't remember was doing some booking of artists in different clubs and he landed a contract for Arstella, Fred Palmer and myself to appear as an attraction in a cabaret called Florida Club which was not far from where I was living, so we opened on the 10th of May. The pianist, bass and drummer of the house band accompanied us and we did three times a half hour each night. The pianist and bassist were good…
